sourceEvidence.label: Browser shopping research and current Nix browser configuration

assessment.summary: Separate cashback-compatible browsing from the protected daily browser and avoid the optional Rakuten extension.

nonNegotiables: uBlock Origin remains enabled in daily browsing
Rakuten cannot observe daily tabs or profile data
Browser security checks remain enabled during checkout
assumptions: Zen remains the preferred daily browser
No measured performance or memory budget was supplied
Cashback attribution requires cookies during the transaction

opportunities.title: Isolate cashback tracking from daily browsing
opportunities.summary: Put the Rakuten-compatible transaction flow in a browser context that cannot observe or weaken daily browsing.
opportunities.diagnosis: Containers isolate site data but not extensions, while the current Nix extension policy applies to every profile in each browser application.

evidence.claim: Rakuten supports a website click-through without its extension, while its extension collects broad browsing and shopping data.
The current shared extension configuration requires uBlock Origin in both Firefox and Zen.
Firefox extension installation is compiled into an application-wide enterprise policy.
A container cannot prevent a broadly permissioned extension in the same profile from observing ordinary tabs.

desiredInvariants: Rakuten code cannot observe daily tabs, URLs, searches, or carts.
uBlock Origin remains enabled without exceptions in daily browsing.
Only the short transaction context accepts affiliate tracking.
The shopping context retains Safe Browsing, certificate validation, HTTPS-Only Mode, and an extension allowlist.

options.title: Daily-browser exceptions
options.summary: Use a shopping container and temporary content-blocking exceptions in the daily profile.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Website click-through avoids the Rakuten extension, but the daily profile still needs filtering exceptions.
Shared required uBlock Origin still needs transaction exceptions.
The application-wide Firefox policy does not change.

tradeoffs.assessment: The daily profile accepts affiliate tracking during exceptions and cannot contain profile-wide extension permissions.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inspect uBlock trusted sites and extension permissions before and after a test trip.

tradeoffs.assessment: Container tabs run in the existing browser and add no planned process.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare page-load behavior in an ordinary tab and Shopping container.

tradeoffs.assessment: No additional browser instance is required.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure browser resident memory with equivalent tab sets.

tradeoffs.assessment: A hostname exception may miss an affiliate redirect and lose attribution.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run a low-value purchase and confirm Rakuten records the trip.

tradeoffs.assessment: The user must manage repeated exceptions and remember to restore them.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Record the number of manual state changes in a complete purchase.

tradeoffs.assessment: The option needs container setup but no extension-policy redesign.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Confirm current profiles can create and persist the Shopping container.

residualRisks: Tracking exceptions affect the daily profile.
An installed Rakuten extension would retain profile-wide access.

workPackages: Create a Shopping container and document the exception workflow.
acceptanceCriteria: A test purchase records cashback and daily filtering is restored afterward.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Remove container assignments and uBlock trusted-site entries.

options.title: Separate Firefox profile
options.summary: Use a distinct Firefox Shopping profile and make extension ownership profile-specific.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Firefox profiles isolate add-ons and browsing data, and the website flow avoids Rakuten's extension.
Required application-wide uBlock Origin must move to profile-specific ownership.
The application-wide policy must permit rather than automatically install profile-specific extensions.

tradeoffs.assessment: Firefox separates profile data and add-ons, keeping shopping state out of the daily profile.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inspect both profiles' add-ons, storage, and history after a transaction.

tradeoffs.assessment: Concurrent profiles may create another browser instance and renderer set.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure launch time and page responsiveness with both profiles running.

tradeoffs.assessment: Concurrent profiles retain separate browser and site state.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare idle resident memory for one and two Firefox profiles.

tradeoffs.assessment: The shopping profile can omit uBlock Origin and follow Rakuten's supported Firefox path.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Verify policy state and complete a low-value eligible purchase.

tradeoffs.assessment: Nix permission and browser installation state may have different owners.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise install, update, disable, removal, and rebuild flows for each profile.

tradeoffs.assessment: The current browser-wide extension compiler cannot express distinct automatic profile installs.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Add contract tests for effective extension membership in both profiles before rollout.

residualRisks: Both profiles share the Firefox application and operating-system account.
A mixed Nix and browser-owned extension model can drift.

workPackages: Add a Shopping profile and allow browser-managed daily extensions without installing them into every profile.
acceptanceCriteria: Personal remains the default, Shopping starts with only Bitwarden, and no separate launcher is installed.
migrationNotes: Nix owns the allowlist while Firefox owns installation and updates in each profile.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Remove the Shopping profile declaration and restore application-wide extension installation.

options.title: Dedicated shopping browser
options.summary: Keep Zen protected for daily research and use a supported browser only for the final purchase flow.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The website flow removes the Rakuten extension and the browser boundary separates transaction state.
uBlock Origin can move from shared membership to the Zen daily-browser group.
Firefox's application-wide policy becomes appropriate when Firefox has one shopping role.
Zen's separate application policy retains daily hardening.
Personal extension groups can encode browser roles without moving personal data into reusable modules.

tradeoffs.assessment: Application-separated profiles and policies keep shopping trackers and blocker exceptions out of Zen.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inspect extension, storage, history, and policy state in both applications after a purchase.

tradeoffs.assessment: Running Zen and the shopping browser concurrently adds another application process tree.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure launch time and checkout responsiveness with Zen open and closed.

tradeoffs.assessment: A second browser retains its own parent and renderer processes.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Record idle and checkout resident memory for Zen alone and both applications.

tradeoffs.assessment: A supported blocker-free browser follows Rakuten's documented compatibility path without repeated toggles.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Complete a low-value eligible purchase and confirm the shopping trip and cashback.

tradeoffs.assessment: A distinct launcher makes the boundary visible and turns cleanup into one explicit action.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Count user actions and verify ordinary links continue to open in Zen.

tradeoffs.assessment: Firefox settings and extension membership must change if it becomes shopping-only.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Evaluate the browser contract and test rollback to the current extension grouping.

residualRisks: Rakuten and merchants still see transaction data, IP address, and device characteristics.
The shopping browser is not a sandbox against compromised native code.
Firefox cannot remain a fully equivalent daily-browser fallback under this role split.

workPackages: Add a visible shopping launcher, split extensions by browser role, configure transaction-safe settings, and add a confirmed reset action.
acceptanceCriteria: Zen retains uBlock Origin, Firefox contains only checkout-safe extensions, ordinary links open in Zen, and a test trip records cashback.
migrationNotes: Do not delete existing Firefox profile data automatically.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Restore shared extension membership and remove shopping-only settings and launcher.

opportunities.recommendation: Keep Personal and Shopping profiles inside Firefox, use Rakuten.com without its extension, and leave Zen as the default browser.

openQuestions: Does a low-value transaction work with Standard tracking protection and no Rakuten extension?
